findings.reason: without a fixture on a plan that still has an implementable section, a node can leave the section-holding branch unedited and still pass every fixture, because a finished plan is not blocked whether or not that half of the rule was written.
findings.text: §3's rule removes an unpassed gate from *both* holding lists when its gated section is done, but all four fixtures assert only "not blocked" on fixtures that have no implementable section; the section-holding half of the edit is measured nowhere, and §3 names that half as live (`_section_gate_blockers` reports it at `reckon/mcp_views.py:2504`, roadmap row key `section_gate_blockers` at `reckon/roadmap.py:3319`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `split_unpassed_gates`, the roadmap ladder, `_derive_lifecycle`, `_blocking`/`_section_gate_blockers`, `unpassed_gate_blockers` and the cited evidence file all resolve at the stated locations.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's four fixtures cover only plans with no implementable section, so neither fixture measures §3's own section-holding change (a gate on a done section inside a plan that still has implementable work), which is the one shape §2's closable short-circuit cannot mask.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the one path §3 relies on, `docs/evidence/archive/a-finished-plan-closes-landed.html`, is a durable repository evidence record, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §3's prose names mechanisms and files, carrying no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §3's stated behaviour matches the code it cites (`not declared - named` returns every unpassed gate as plan-holding; a failed closed gate stays unpassed), and it names the production callers the edit reaches (roadmap ladder, `_derive_lifecycle`, the two MCP readers) rather than assuming a path.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable, the gate-holding rule in `split_unpassed_gates`.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s3 declares no depends-on, and the followup states §3 can start at once; the readers and inputs §3 names all exist.
